title: Bank of America sends stark warning on Tripadvisor
detail:
Bank of America sends stark warning on Tripadvisor
Faizan Farooque, Celine Provini
Mon, November 9, 2026 at 3:33 PM CST 6 min read
TRIP
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

It should be enjoyable to plan a family trip.

However, anybody who has spent an evening researching hotels, reading reviews, and looking for kid-friendly activities will attest to how quickly the process can become taxing.

A hotel seems flawless until someone brings up unstated costs. A sightseeing trip seems like a great idea until someone else tells you about a bad experience. Selecting the ideal vacation suddenly seems like a full-time job.

Tripadvisor has helped millions of tourists make their choices for years.

The business that created the well-known website is now dealing with its own issues.

Bank of America has downgraded Tripadvisor (TRIP) to Underperform from Buy, slashing its stock-price target to $8 from $15.

The warning comes as the company's two most senior executives are scheduled to leave, bookings are falling, and profitability has been disappointing.

However, something deeper is taking place.

The way consumers look for hotels, compare locations, and find things to do on vacation is being transformed by artificial intelligence. The web traffic Tripadvisor has historically relied on is therefore at risk.

This raises a more significant question: Will conventional travel websites remain helpful as AI takes over more trip-planning tasks?

According to Bank of America, investors may find the shift to be far more costly than anticipated.

Why Bank of America sees a bigger problem for Tripadvisor

Bank of America analyst Nafeesa Gupta downgraded Tripadvisor on Nov. 5, arguing that slowing growth and management changes have made the company's recovery more uncertain. The bank reduced its price target to $8 from $15, a nearly 47% cut.

The research report found that Tripadvisor's third-quarter revenue fell 11%, exceeding management's guidance for 7% to 10%.

The company's sales of $436.4 million were less than Wall Street's estimate of $453 million. In contrast to the roughly $89 million experts had predicted, adjusted profits before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization came in at $71.1 million.

Tripadvisor's third-quarter earnings release confirmed the results.

However, Bank of America's worries go beyond a single underwhelming quarter.

The company identified three main issues, including declining revenue, disruption from shifting internet search, and concern about the company's upcoming leadership change. The report's central warning summarizes its assessment: "Growth slows, execution risk rises."

Due to pressure on its conventional online travel operations, Tripadvisor's hotels and other companies reported a 23% drop in revenue during the quarter.

title: Target faces 2027 sales slowdown and rising cost pressures, Bank of America warns

Target faces 2027 sales slowdown and rising cost pressures, Bank of America warns

BAC
TGT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Target faces 2027 sales slowdown and rising cost pressures, Bank of America warns Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America has reiterated its cautious stance on Target Corp (NYSE:TGT) despite raising its price objective slightly, warning that slowing sales growth and persistent costs could challenge the retailer in 2027.

The broker increased its price objective to $141 from $140, maintaining a valuation multiple of 15 times estimated earnings, but highlighted risks to earnings forecasts and the sustainability of recent comparable sales growth.

Target has delivered an improvement in sales this year, supported by merchandising initiatives and stronger performance in categories including food, entertainment and beauty.

Bank of America expects these initiatives to support comparable sales growth of 4% in the third quarter, up from its previous forecast of 3%.

However, it cut its third-quarter earnings per share forecast by $0.09 to $2.08, reflecting expectations of weaker gross margins and higher selling, general and administrative expenses.

The broker sees a more challenging operating environment emerging as Target faces tougher year-on-year comparisons, higher freight costs and increased promotional activity across the retail sector.

It also believes Target has less flexibility to reduce administrative and operating expenses than other retailers because it needs to maintain investment spending to support sustainable sales growth.

Category performance remains mixed, with food and beverages, which account for 23% of sales, outperforming the wider market.

Entertainment and discretionary merchandise, representing 15% of sales, has also benefited from initiatives such as Pokémon trading card releases, although Bank of America warned that slowing demand for cards could weaken customer acquisition.

Beauty, accounting for 13% of sales, remains a strong category, supported by the launch of Target Beauty Studio.

Apparel and home, each representing 15% of revenue, present greater challenges, with the broker questioning whether improvements in clothing will arrive before 2027.

It also highlighted Walmart's stronger competitive position in apparel compared with five years ago, limiting Target's ability to raise prices.

The broker expects a broader overhaul of Target's home merchandise range next year, while household essentials, accounting for 17% of sales, should remain relatively stable.

The valuation debate centres on whether Target can deliver earnings above the market's financial 2027 consensus forecast of $9.65 per share.

Bank of America forecasts $9.40, leaving it below consensus despite its improved sales outlook.

The company's strong start to the early holiday shopping season could support the shares in the near term, but the broker remains concerned about the balance between sales growth, margins and investment spending.

Investing.com - Bank of America has downgraded three European semiconductor stocks in a single sweep, cutting VAT Group to Neutral from Buy, Comet to Underperform from Buy, and Inficon to Underperform from Neutral, warning that high memory exposure leaves all three vulnerable if the chip cycle turns.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The moves follow BofA's downgrade of Siltronic to Underperform in the prior week, bringing the firm's tally of recent European semis cuts to four names. Accordingly, a deteriorating memory cycle has historically hit high-fixed-cost equipment suppliers hardest, and BofA judges VAT and Comex no longer warrant Buy ratings.

"Rarely has the market been as polarised between universally bullish bottom-up indicators and bearish top-down indicators," the firm's analyst wrote.

Company-level order books and management commentary across European semicap names remain constructive, yet BofA sees mounting macro-level threats: potential financing stress for so-called neoclouds and tightening regulatory scrutiny of data-center buildouts.

U.S. cloud capital expenditure is currently running at a $300 billion per quarter rate ($1.2 trillion annualized), heading toward $375 billion per quarter in calendar 2027.

However, BofA calculates that if the current rate marks an intermediate peak, that implies roughly 20% potential downside versus CY27 capex expectations — equivalent, by its math, to a roughly 10 GW headwind against its 40-plus GW baseline deployment assumption for 2027 data centers (using a $40 billion per GW capex average across merchant and custom chips).

On the valuation front, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) has underperformed the S&P 500 by more than 37% since its June peak, which BofA identifies as the largest such relative drawdown in the past 20 years.

That dislocation has pushed European semicap stocks to roughly 10x EV/EBIT turns below their median multiples on CY27 consensus estimates, while EU analog names trade 1.6x turns below their medians, per BofA.

Yet the firm is not broadly bearish. BofA retains Buy ratings on ASML, ASM International, and BE Semiconductor's peer TPRO, noting all three trade 0.5x to 4.0x below their five-year historical EV/EBIT multiples.

Investing.com -- Bank of America sees a potential recovery in semiconductor stocks in early 2027 as improving U.S. policy clarity, corporate buybacks and relatively attractive valuations help ease concerns over artificial intelligence spending, although investors may need to wait for earnings estimate cuts before the sector finds a durable bottom.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) has already fallen 37% from its recent peak, compared with an average correction of 32% during previous downturns. The bank said indiscriminate selling driven by fears of slowing AI capital expenditure could begin to run its course by early 2027, with congressional policy developments and share repurchases helping restore confidence.

Semiconductor stocks trade at 13.7 times forward earnings, a 22% discount to the S&P 500's 17.7 times multiple. A return to the historical trough valuation of around 12 times earnings would imply at most another 12% downside, according to BofA. The bank also highlighted buyback support from Lam Research, which has a $25 billion programme, ongoing repurchases by Nvidia and Micron's planned buyback start on December 9.

Previous semiconductor downturns suggest the sector typically declines six to nine months ahead of the fundamental earnings turn, before recovering as earnings estimate reductions become reflected in valuations. The SOX has gained an average of 42% during previous recoveries after those cuts were priced in.

BofA sees the late-June 2026 market peak as a potential signal that earnings estimate reductions could begin in the first quarter of 2027, as companies adjust second-half spending plans. However, the bank cautioned that cheaper valuations alone may not be sufficient to restore confidence, with actual earnings cuts likely needed to establish a sustainable floor.

AI spending remains the biggest swing factor

U.S. cloud capital expenditure is currently running at an annualised rate of about $1.2 trillion, with forecasts pointing to more than $1.5 trillion in 2027. If spending stabilises at current levels rather than accelerating, it would represent a roughly 20% downside against 2027 capital expenditure expectations.
